overclaims: The release identifies June 16–July 19 as the survey period and cautions that subgroup uncertainty exceeds the full-sample margin of error.
checks.note: The rationale figures (69/54/53%) and the fieldwork dates match e2. The public excerpt for e2 is cut to 'oppose new local data centers.', which drops the subject and every party figure, so it no longer supports the claim on its face. The e2 explanation says the release warns that subgroup uncertainty exceeds the full-sample margin of error. The quoted text contains no such warning, and the limitation on subgroup uncertainty relies on it. The cited text is the Phys.org reproduction, not the original release.

The rationale numbers match the page 14 table: 48.9 to 60.6, +11.8, CI +6.9 to +16.6, and the within-person CI +9.0 to +16.1 excludes zero. The limitations are fair. The public excerpt for e1, 'a statistically significant shift.', is cut from a conditional method note ('a confidence interval that excludes zero indicates a statistically significant shift'). Read alone, it looks like the report states a finding. The excerpt should quote the opposition row or the full sentence.
